name: Banh trang phoi suong
summary: A two-layer Trảng Bàng rice sheet, toasted over a peanut-shell fire until small bubbles rise, then rested briefly in the dew until it softens without going damp. You roll it at the table with boiled pork or young beef, a basket of garden and forest herbs, and a sauce that runs sour and sweet.
origin: Trảng Bàng, Tây Ninh. The ward has been phường Trảng Bàng since 1 July 2025.
history: The craft entered the national intangible-heritage list in 2015 by the tourism information center’s date, and in 2016 by the provincial craft site’s.
Some Trảng Bàng producers hold OCOP 4-star and 5-star ratings for their sheets.
texture: The sheet is two thin layers, pale after the fire, with small bubbles across it.
The town puts the dew rest at one or two minutes; the 2024 national tourism article says short and near dawn, or the sheet goes damp.
taste: The town dips it in fish sauce with garlic and chili, the national rural-tourism site names tamarind fish sauce, and Gia Huỳnh kitchens serve sauces that run sour and sweet.
howToEat: Lay a sheet flat, add boiled pork or boiled young beef and a handful of herbs, roll it, and dip. The herbs can include forest leaves such as mặt trăng, trâm ổi, chùm mòi, quế vị, cóc, rau nhái, and lộc vừng.
The young-beef roll adds fresh rice noodles and leaves like quế vị, lá cách, đọt cóc, sao nhái, and cải trời, dipped in mắm nêm or mixed fish sauce.
where: Sit down in khu phố Gia Huỳnh. The yards where sheets are poured, dried, and toasted are in khu phố Lộc Du; go in the morning if you want the dew racks.
seoTitle: Banh trang phoi suong in Tay Ninh
seoDescription: Trảng Bàng rice paper, toasted over a peanut-shell fire and rested in the dew, rolled with boiled pork or young beef and forest herbs.
